subject: Corelytics performance readiness: SLOs, concurrency, and cost levers
messages:

Subject: Corelytics performance readiness: SLOs, concurrency, and cost levers

Hi Priya / Devon —

Thanks again for the productive call today. Quick recap and the concrete asks we agreed to:

1) Target SLOs you asked us to qualify against:
   - P95 end-to-end generation latency: <= 250 ms (interactive UI flows)
   - Sustained throughput target: 600 requests/minute (≈10 rps) with 2k token average response
   - Peak concurrency headroom: ability to sustain 1.5x expected peak for 10m bursts
   - Streaming: chunked token delivery for progressive UI renders, 1 token latency budget <= 30 ms

2) Workloads we should assume for qualification:
   - Mix: 70% short responses (<=256 tokens), 30% long responses (avg 2k tokens)
   - 60% of requests will be cache-friendly (repeated prompts / system prefixes)

3) Next steps we committed to on the call:
   - Redwood: deliver an SLO matrix and a short cost/latency tradeoff analysis (we'll attach a first-pass spreadsheet).
   - Redwood: run a targeted pilot with our dedicated pools for 24h to validate burst headroom and streaming latency.
   - Corelytics: share a representative prompt set and a sample of 200 production traces (anonymized).

I attached a draft SLO matrix and our quantization profile brief for reference. Ben and Karthik are looping in ops/serving to scope the pilot.

Would you be able to share the sample prompts/traces by Friday (2026-12-04)? If that works we'll aim to run the pilot the following week.

Best,
Aisha
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Corelytics_SLO_matrix_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood_quant_profiles.pdf (summary), demo-recording-20261130.mp4 (30MB video stub)

Subject: Re: Corelytics performance readiness: SLOs, concurrency, and cost levers

Thanks Aisha — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side after reviewing the SLO draft: 

- The 250 ms p95 target is for the UI read path only (search + summary). For background async jobs (batch re-ranking) we can accept higher latency (up to 2s).
- For streaming, we need the first token to show within 120 ms on cold start; after that steady-state chunking should meet your 30 ms per token budget.
- Our peak is more bursty than average — we have scheduled marketing blasts that can create 3x traffic for ~5 minutes. Can you validate burst + fallback behavior for 3x as well?

We will upload the anonymized traces and a 150-prompt sample to the Drive link you shared by EOD Friday.

Also: budgeting question for the pilot — can you provide a short estimate for the 24h dedicated-run cost across the three model variants you mentioned on the call? A ballpark helps us fast-track the PO.

Best,
Priya Shah
VP Product, Corelytics
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <pshah@corelytics.com>, Devon Rogers <devon.rogers@corelytics.com>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2026 02:14:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Corelytics performance readiness: SLOs, concurrency, and cost levers

Hi Priya — quick technical reply to the burst + cost questions (following up from our ops sync).

1) Burst handling and graceful fallback:
   - Strategy: run pilot on a dedicated pool + reserve a smaller cross-tenant burst pool for 3x spikes. If primary pool saturates we automatically route to a lower-cost, highly-quantized model variant.
   - Expected behavior: slightly higher per-token latency on fallback (~+30-80 ms) but service remains available and streaming keeps delivering chunks.

2) Models & quantization profiles to validate in pilot:
   - Variant A: redwood-2-school-13B (fp16) — baseline quality, moderate cost
   - Variant B: redwood-2-school-13B-int8 (8-bit quantized) — ~1.6x throughput improvement, small quality delta on long-form generation
   - Variant C: redwood-2-compact-7B-int4 (aggressive int4) — ~2.5x throughput, best cost profile, recommended for degraded-fallback and high-concurrency bursts

3) Levers we will exercise during 24h run (what we'll measure):
   - Continuous micro-batching (adaptive batch windows tuned to maintain 250ms p95)
   - Prefix/KV caching for ~60% cacheable requests (we expect ~35-50% token cost reduction there)
   - Quantization mixes: measure quality delta on a 50-prompt probe set and tokens/sec improvements
   - Streaming chunk size: tune to hit first-token budgets while maximizing GPU utilization

4) Ballpark pilot cost (24 hours, dedicated pool + burst reserve):
   - Variant A baseline run: ~$6,500
   - Variant B (int8) run: ~$4,100
   - Variant C (int4) run: ~$2,200

These are preliminary; we'll include a per-token and per-concurrent-request breakdown in the SLO matrix. I'll attach a short one-pager (redwood_quant_profiles.pdf) summarizing the quantization tradeoffs.

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Corelytics performance readiness: SLOs, concurrency, and cost levers — next steps and pilot plan

Thanks Priya — perfect. We got the traces and prompts this morning; Ben and Karthik will begin ingesting and setting up the pilot harness. Couple of operational notes and confirmed next steps: 

- Pilot scope: 24h dedicated run + 2h soak at 3x for burst validation (we'll simulate the 5-minute marketing blasts and a 10-minute sustained spike).
- Success criteria: p95 UI path <= 250 ms (target), first-token <= 120 ms cold-start, streaming chunk steady-state <= 30 ms per token, no unrecoverable errors during 3x bursts.
- Deliverables by end of pilot: SLO matrix with measured numbers, cost per 1k tokens and per-concurrency-hour, model-quality delta report, and a short runbook for production cutover.

Timing: We can start the pilot as early as Monday 2026-12-06 if you approve the PO. Give us a thumbs up and we'll submit the pilot estimate formally (Ben will share an itemized quote by EOD today).

Thanks — looking forward to validating this with you.

Regards,
Aisha Rahman
